title: How much of a lesson is review
statement: How much of a lesson should be review, and whether that share should change with the lesson's place in a unit, is unsettled.
example: One course's documents give about 70:30 review to new for middle lessons, about 70:30 new to review, and about 90:10 review to new.
detail: A Grade 4 reading course's generation contract replaced a literal 90:10 review budget with a banded one: middle lessons about 70:30 review to new, openers about 50:50 because little has been taught, and synthesis or transfer lessons about 90:10. The same course's pedagogy notes and foundations document say about 70:30 new to review, and its sequencing brief sets within-unit spacing at about 90% review and 10% new across interleaved tracks, as does a Grade 1 plan. The documents agree that review runs in tracks beside the new material and differ on the share, and nothing measured which share helps learners.

evidence.quote: Middle lessons ~70:30 (review:new); openers/BUILD ~50:50 (little prior; say so); synthesis/transfer ~90:10.
